newsitem.title: CHINA: Ten killed after Moslems riots in Xinjiang.
newsitem.headline: Ten killed after Moslems riots in Xinjiang.

text.p: At least 10 people were killed and several arrested when more than 1,000 Moslems in China's restive northwestern region of Xinjiang rioted last week, Chinese sources said on Monday.
The riot erupted last Wednesday in the mainly Moslem region after a Chinese policeman tried to arrest a man of the Uighur minority, said one source who asked not to be identified.
"The police tried to arrest a Uighur criminal suspect but the suspect and his family resisted arrest," the source told Reuters by telephone.
"The scene attracted neighbours and onlookers and the crowd swelled to more than 1,000 and turned into rioting," he said.
"The police were called in and fired teargas to dispel the crowd."
More than 10 people, including at least one police officer, were killed and an unknown number injured in the rioting, the source said.
The Hong Kong-based Ming Pao newspaper said the bodies of those killed had been set on fire by rioters. The Chinese-language daily put the number of injured at around 100.
The newspaper described the rioting as one of the biggest ethnic disturbances in China since the communists came to power in 1949.
"One police officer was stabbed to death," the source said, adding that several people had been arrested in connection with the rioting.
Xinjiang, considered by many Chinese to be a wild frontier territory, has a long history of ethnic clashes between the native Uighur population and China's Han majority.
